messages:
Maya: Heads up — after the rolling update to the dedicated pool around 08:12 UTC, the Dedicated Capacity dashboard shows 0 GPUs for the us-west-1 cluster even though nodes are up in k8s. Console screenshot attached in thread. :eyes:

Ali: Confirming, saw a customer escalations ticket too — they reported capacity alerts firing. Metrics page for 'node_gpu_count' is blank for that pool.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout/dedicated-pool-us-west completed at 2025-11-27T08:11:53Z (image: infra/dedicated:2025.11.27)

Ryan (oncall): Ok, quick checklist: 1) kubectl get nodes 2) curl inventory svc 3) check inventory-sync logs 4) grafana datasource scrape status. Can someone run the first two?

Maya: Running kubectl now — nodes look Ready and have GPU allocatable set
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-us-west -o wide
NAME                                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-1.compute     Ready    <none>   5d    v1.27.3
ip-10-0-23-11.us-west-1.compute     Ready    <none>   5d    v1.27.3
```
Allocatable shows nvidia.com/gpu=8 on both nodes.

Ali: Running inventory API check against internal inventory service
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inventory.internal.api/v1/nodes?pool=dedicated-us-west | jq '.nodes | map({name:.name, gpu:.labels["redwood.com/gpu_count"]})'
```
Response: nodes returned but the label redwood.com/gpu_count is null for both nodes. inventory-sync-bot then: inventory-sync failed to map labels during last sync (08:12:07) due to key mismatch.

inventory-sync-bot: ERROR inventory-sync: unable to map node label redwood.com/gpu_count for node ip-10-0-12-34; found labels: ["nvidia.com/gpu","node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"]

Ryan (oncall): That explains dashboard — the dashboard queries the inventory DB field derived from redwood.com/gpu_count. During the rolling update the node-agent started exporting the standard nvidia.com/gpu label but our inventory mapper expects the legacy redwood.com/gpu_count label. Looks like the node-agent image bumped to 2.0 which dropped the legacy label.

Maya: Confirmed in node-agent change log: v2.0 removes redwood label in favor of standard k8s resource name. The rollout inadvertently updated node-agents in the dedicated pool. Oops.

Ali: Short-term mitigation: we can restart inventory-sync to force re-ingest with a mapping shim that reads nvidia.com/gpu if redwood.com/gpu_count missing. I can patch the job now and restart.

Ryan (oncall): Steps to apply quick fix (approved):
1) apply a hotfix configmap mapping in infra namespace (inventory-mapper: add fallback key)
2) rollout restart deployment/inventory-sync -n infra
3) check inventory logs and Grafana panel for counts to return

Maya: Patching configmap and restarting now.
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap inventory-mapper --patch '{"data":{"fallback_label":"nvidia.com/gpu"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/inventory-sync
```

inventory-sync-bot: INFO inventory-sync: reconcile started at 2025-11-27T08:18:10Z

Ali: Logs show mapper used fallback_label and populated gpu_count from nvidia.com/gpu for both nodes.

Maya: Grafana panel shows counts recovering — was 0, now reads 16 total GPUs for the pool. Refresh delay ~90s.

Ryan (oncall): Good. Root cause timeline: node-agent v2.0 removed legacy label -> rolling update applied node-agent across dedicated pool -> inventory-sync expected legacy label -> dashboards queried DB and returned 0 GPUs. Impact: dashboards + any autoscaling decisions that use inventory field while mismatch present.

Sylvia: Need a postmortem + followups: 1) Make inventory mapper tolerant of multiple label formats (done as hotfix) 2) Add unit/integration test so label schema changes in node-agent trigger CI failure 3) Add a small Grafana alert for inventory-db vs k8s resource mismatch (delta > 1 node or >10% GPUs) 4) Communicate to customers who saw alerts. Assigning to eng-platform backlog.

Maya: i'll open the postmortem draft and link the rollout PR that bumped node-agent. Tagging Ryan and Ali.

Ali: Customer ticket updated — informed them we restored dashboard counts and are doing root-cause + proactive changes.

Ryan (oncall): For the record, immediate remediation steps we took: patched inventory-mapper config, restarted inventory-sync, monitored logs and grafana. Time-to-recover ≈ 6 minutes.

Maya: Follow-up action items in backlog: 1) revert node-agent auto-update for dedicated pools until compatibility matrix checked 2) add integration test to infra pipeline 3) run a one-off job to backfill any nodes that missed label during rollout.

Sylvia: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule a deep dive with infra/release tomorrow to tighten rollout checks. :white_check_mark:
